# iPastoralist

**An R package for vegetation data analysis, phytopastoral assessment,
and phytosociological classification.**

*iPastoralist* provides tools for processing, analyzing, and classifying
plant communities, with particular emphasis on grassland and pasture
vegetation.

The package supports botanical data collected using both **point-quadrat
(point-intercept)** and **phytosociological** survey methods,
integrating biodiversity assessment, ecological indicators, pastoral
evaluation, and numerical vegetation classification.

## Main features

### 1. Vegetation data preparation and conversion

- **Point-quadrat data processing:** convert species frequency of
  occurrence into relative abundance and estimated percentage cover,
  including optional treatment of occasional species
  ([`vegetation_abundance()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/vegetation_abundance.md)).
- **Phytosociological data conversion:** transform visually estimated
  species cover into Braun-Blanquet, Van der Maarel, and numerical
  cover-abundance scales
  ([`PhytoCover()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/PhytoCover.md)).

### 2. Vegetation characterization

- **Biodiversity assessment:** calculate species richness, Shannon
  diversity, Effective Number of Species, and evenness
  ([`biodiversity()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/biodiversity.md)).
- **Pastoral Value:** assess the forage potential of grassland and
  pasture vegetation
  ([`pastoral_value()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/pastoral_value.md)).
- **Ecological indicator values:** calculate Ellenberg and Landolt
  community-level indices, with optional abundance weighting
  ([`ecological_indexes()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/ecological_indexes.md)).
- **Floristic composition:** extract the most abundant species for
  individual vegetation surveys
  ([`first_ten_species()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/first_ten_species.md)).

### 3. Vegetation classification and interpretation

*iPastoralist* provides tools supporting numerical vegetation
classification and the characterization of resulting vegetation groups.

Main functionalities include:

- **Numerical classification:** identify vegetation groups based on
  floristic similarity.
- **Classification evaluation:** compare alternative partitions and
  support the selection of the number of vegetation groups.
- **Species characterization:** identify diagnostic, constant, dominant,
  and companion species.
- **Synoptic vegetation tables:** summarize species frequencies and
  floristic differences among vegetation groups.
- **Phytopastoral interpretation:** characterize grassland and pasture
  types according to their botanical composition, ecological properties,
  and pastoral characteristics.
- **Phytosociological interpretation:** support the identification and
  comparison of vegetation units and their possible attribution to
  established syntaxonomic schemes.

These tools facilitate **reproducible vegetation classification
workflows**, combining numerical analyses with ecological and
expert-based interpretation.

## Installation

Install *iPastoralist* directly from GitHub using the `pak` package:

\`\`\`r id=“m0vzq8” \# Install pak (if needed) install.packages(“pak”)

# Install iPastoralist

pak::pak(“MarcoPittarello/iPastoralist”)

# Load the package

library(iPastoralist) \`\`\`

## Documentation

Detailed descriptions of the functions, methodological explanations, and
examples are available in the package documentation.

- **Website and function reference:** [iPastoralist
  website](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/)
- **Introduction and tutorials:** available in the website’s Articles
  section.
- **Source code:** [GitHub
  repository](https://github.com/MarcoPittarello/iPastoralist)

# Package index

## All functions

- [`PhytoCover()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/PhytoCover.md)
  : Transform visually estimated species cover to cover-abundance values
- [`biodiversity()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/biodiversity.md)
  : Biodiversity indexes
- [`clustGroupAggregate()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/clustGroupAggregate.md)
  : Computation of means for cluster groups (aggregate)
- [`clustGroupAggregate2()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/clustGroupAggregate2.md)
  : Computation of means for cluster groups (aggregate)
- [`clustOrder()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/clustOrder.md)
  : Individuation of the position and/or the group of appartenance of
  surveys in a dendrogram
- [`clustOrder_twspn()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/clustOrder_twspn.md)
  : Survey order and terminal groups of an ecan TWINSPAN classification
- [`denspe()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/denspe.md)
  : Matrix for cluster analysis with surveys labelled with the first
  species ordered by decreasing abundance
- [`denspe_twspn()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/denspe_twspn.md)
  : Label TWINSPAN Vegetation Surveys with Their Most Abundant Species
- [`ecological_indexes()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/ecological_indexes.md)
  : Computation of Ecological indicators (Landolt, Ellenberg) from
  vertical point-quadrat method surveys
- [`ecological_indexesPHYTO()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/ecological_indexesPHYTO.md)
  : Computation of Ecological indicators (Landolt, Ellenberg) from
  phytosociological surveys
- [`export_synoptic()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/export_synoptic.md)
  : Export a Phytosociological Synoptic Table to Excel
- [`first_ten_species()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/first_ten_species.md)
  : First ten species for dendrogram
- [`first_ten_species_twspn()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/first_ten_species_twspn.md)
  : Most abundant species per survey with TWINSPAN classification
- [`iPastoralist`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/iPastoralist.md)
  : iPastoralist: Tools for pastoralist survey analysis
- [`maxFusionLevel()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/maxFusionLevel.md)
  : Identify the Optimal Number of Clusters Based on Maximum Fusion
  Height
- [`nameGroups()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/nameGroups.md)
  : Name vegetation groups based on dominant species
- [`pastoral_value()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/pastoral_value.md)
  : Computation of Pastoral Value (PV)
- [`plotClustAggregate()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/plotClustAggregate.md)
  : Plot dendrograms and (optionally) aggregated cluster summaries
- [`plotClustAggregate_twspn()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/plotClustAggregate_twspn.md)
  : Fit TWINSPAN and plot its dendrogram using the iPastoralist layout
- [`synoptic_table()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/synoptic_table.md)
  : Build a Synoptic Table of Diagnostic, Constant and Dominant Species
- [`tb_pca_plot()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/tb_pca_plot.md)
  : Exploratory transformation-based PCA of vegetation communities
- [`twinspan_optimclass_ecan()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/twinspan_optimclass_ecan.md)
  : Select Vegetation Clusters Using Modified TWINSPAN and OptimClass
- [`vegetation_abundance()`](https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/reference/vegetation_abundance.md)
  : Transform Frequency of occurrence (FO) to Species relative abundance
  (SRA) or Species percentage cover(%SC)
